The '''Temple district''', also known as the '''Temple Precinct''' or '''Temple Court''', was a series of city blocks on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] jointly overseen by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] until [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] when the [[Declaration of a New Order]] dissolved the Order and the district was seized by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Established circa [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] when the Republic donated the [[Sacred spire/Legends|sacred spire]] to the Order for their participation in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], the early Jedi set up small facilities which eventually expanded over the [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] and was later known as the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. Following the district's total ruin during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], it was reconstructed under the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] and home to the [[New Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] once more.

==History==
Following the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] granted the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] use of the [[Sacred spire/Legends|sacred spire]], a holy site for the local [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] located to the north of the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District]], for the construction of a great bastion from which they could repel the threats that would plague the Republic.<ref name="SWCL" /> However, much to the disappointment of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], the Order simply established a small meditation enclave, unlike to the great fortresses on [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] or [[Falang Minor]].<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

Yet once a group of [[Four Masters/Legends|Four Masters]] pioneered the construction of a [[Jedi academy]] on the planet, the area became more developed and began to take the shape seen across the city-planet. The area around the mountain was part of the ancient city built on the crust. To bring the area up to the crust, the builders of the Temple sunk giant pylons deep into the planet to support the [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] tall bloc that would serve as platform for the Temple. Giant heaps of trash would accumulate around the pylons over the centuries as the area was abandoned for use by the Order. Buildings were erected on the platform resting atop the pylons, becoming occupied by citizens of [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]].<ref name="LJU">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref> At long last, the expanding area reached the top level where the Temple was to rest. For kilometers, the city blocs did not rise beyond that of Sacred Spire, ensuring that the Temple could be seen from great distances.<ref name="SWCL" /> The top of the bloc that encompassed the main portion of the Sacred Spire was landscaped and came to be known as the Temple Court, dotted with [[Bronzium/Legends|bronzium]] statues of great Jedi Masters.<ref name="Deceived" />

[[File:JediTemple-Deceived.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], the center point of the district]]

In [[3653 BBY]], the Temple suffered its first great tragedy. The resurgent [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] emerged from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and began the onslaught that would come to be known as the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]. Greatly damaged and left abandoned, the Senate deemed reconstruction too expensive for a war time budget, forcing the Order to relocate to its homeworld, [[Tython/Legends|Tython]].<ref name="Deceived" /> Eventually, the district and Temple came to be reoccupied no later than [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] and the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]].<ref name="DB:ROT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>

While the Jedi Temple had finished expanding, the district was largely undeveloped below its "surface", or the highest level. Below the Temple Court and in neighboring city blocs, the Order built training facilities and hangar bays that serviced the Temple. Additionally, a [[Spaceport tower/Legends|mooring tower]] was built to accommodate larger ships arriving at the Temple.<ref name="SWCL" /> Sublevel [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]] were built for personal transports as well as for the delivery craft that supplied the Order's members with food that could not be grown at the Temple.<ref name="CWG:S">''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Stealth]]''</ref><ref name="ROTSN">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Water and electricity were pumped through the district to the Temple and its other facilities by the Republic and all future governments, while back-up generators could sustain the complex for several weeks.<ref name="FOTJB">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]''</ref>

The district would continue to service the Order and the local Coruscanti that occupied the areas not used by the Order. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] which began in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Temple district saw more activity as the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] made use of some of the sublevel hangars. Additional facilities were built to support the influx of military supplies moving in and out of the Temple, including several [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolifts]] and new hangars.<ref name="LJU" />

When the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the Republic was revealed to be the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], the Order's leaders [[Showdown on Coruscant|attempted to arrest him]], but failed in the attempt. In order to wipe out the Order, Sidious sent the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], under the command of [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], to [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|subjugate]] the Temple. Suffering damage wrought by [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transports]], the district was completely locked down and sealed by order of the first Galactic Empire's leader, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] Palpatine.<ref name="RCN">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> Government buildings were occupied by clones, while the museum district was bombed. Many of the residents and business owners fled the fighting on fight, never to return to their properties.<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> Promoting [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] propaganda implementing the Order in a [[Treason/Legends|treasonous]] plot to overthrow the Republic, [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Marcellin Wessel]] compiled a [[Casualty Report: Order 66|report]] in which the public would be "informed" of the ways in which the Jedi planned to take the reins of liberty. Within, Moff Wessel described the [[Order 66/Legends|execution]] of Jedi [[Whie Malreaux/Legends|Whie Malreaux]], who had been in the process of [[Mind trick/Legends|manipulating]] the minds of the district's citizens.<ref name="O66" />

Lying abandoned throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the district would eventually fall into utter disrepair during the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|occupation]] of Coruscant by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]].<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref> Several years later following the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance's]] [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar|retaking]] of the capitol, [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Cal Omas]] donated a [[New Jedi Temple|new Temple]] to the [[New Jedi Order|reformed Jedi Order]] in thanks for their sacrifices during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. Built by the [[Reconstruction Authority]], the Temple and district were meticulously restored to their state before the Galactic Empire dismantled the Order. In an attempt to demonstrate the alliance between the [[Galactic Alliance Senate|Senate]], Order, and the Yuuzhan Vong, the Authority created several public areas around the Temple bloc. On the Temple's west side, that which contained the main entrance and the broad [[Processional Way/Legends|Processional Way]], the Authority erected [[Fellowship Plaza]] as a way of connecting the Temple and the [[Galactic Justice Center]] which loomed two blocs away.<ref name="FOTJO">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref> Several kilometers to the north of the Temple was the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]] and the newly erected [[Unity Green]] and [[Liberation Lake]] occupied the nearby blocs.<ref name="DNI" /> Additional security was added to the Temple bloc's outer walls which allowed evacuation routes into the neighboring blocs as well as into the [[Skylane/Legends|skylanes]] that separated the kilometers-tall structures.<ref name="LOTFE">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref>

In [[43 ABY]], Knight [[Jysella Horn]], who was overcome with an [[Force psychosis|enigmatic madness]] inflicting Knights at random, darted across the district having escaped the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]]. Leaving her pursuers behind her, Horn's fellow Jedi [[Yaqeel Saav'etu]] and [[Bazel Warv]] attempted to stop her before she hurt the pedestrians who milled about shops and courtyards in the district. Unable to detain Horn, the ill Jedi was ultimately arrested by [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Forces]] and frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] per instruction from Chief of State [[Natasi Daala]]. Shortly after, Jedi Saav'etu and Warv were walking from Fellowship Plaza when they contracted the same illness and had to be detained by Jedi [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] in a speeder garage. Hoping to avoid further arrests by the government, Jedi [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] devised a plan to evacuate the infected Jedi aboard [[FloatVan]]s docked in lower level hangars and transport them to the [[Jedi Academy (Shedu Maad)|Jedi facility]] in the [[Transitory Mists]]. With the help of Jedi [[Avinoam Arelis]] and [[Jaden Korr]], Solo was successful in getting the infected Jedi away from Coruscant, despite the interference by [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] stationed at the [[Krabbis Inn]] under Fellowship Plaza.<ref name="FOTJO" /> With the Order not cooperating with the Alliance, Chief Daala ordered the district's water and electrical supply to be turned off until the time when they wished to submit to her authority.<ref name="FOTJB" />

==Layout==
[[File:Chris_Trevas_ItWoE2_map.png|thumb|right|200px|The city blocks surronding the Temple Ziggurat.]]
The Temple district was a Coruscant administrative district jointly controlled by the galactic government and the Jedi Order. While the residents within the district answered to the laws laid down by the government, the Jedi had sovereign control of the Jedi Temple.<ref name="FOTJB" /> Made up of several city blocs, the district could be split up into two distinct parts: the city block upon which the Temple rested and all the other public, private, and residential spaces that surrounded it. A busy region of the city, the Precinct was home to hundreds of private residential blocks, an entertainment district, a museum and education district, and commercial districts with shops and restaurants catering to the wealthy bureaucrats that lived in the area.<ref name="NoP" />

First seeing development circa [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the area on the slopes of and around the [[Sacred spire/Legends|Sacred spire]] would grow steadily upward until each bloc's roof reached "surface level", creating a great flat plain around the Temple. Largely remaining low to the tops of the buildings roofs, later construction was largely done below the upper surface,<ref name="SWCL" /> with the exception of the [[Mooring tower/Legends|mooring towers]] built near and around the Temple complex.<ref name="AOTC" />
